recent_posts.title: Scaling cloud and AI: Microsoft Azure’s commitment to Europe’s digital future
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft is significantly expanding Azure datacenter regions across Europe to meet accelerating cloud and AI demand. The expansion covers Northern Europe (Sweden, Denmark, Finland, Norway), Southern Europe (Spain, Italy, Greece), Western Europe (UK with $30B investment, Belgium), and Central Europe (Germany, Austria, Poland). Key themes include sovereign cloud solutions for data residency and regulatory compliance, sustainable datacenter design, multi-region architecture guidance, and AI skills programs. Customer examples span public sector, manufacturing, financial services, healthcare, and energy sectors.

recent_posts.title: Azure IaaS: Defense in depth built on secure-by-design principles
recent_posts.summary: Azure IaaS security is built on two reinforcing pillars: defense-in-depth architecture and Microsoft's Secure Future Initiative (SFI) principles. Defense in depth spans hardware root-of-trust, hypervisor-enforced VM isolation, network segmentation, encrypted storage, and continuous monitoring. SFI principles translate into: secure by design (TPMs, measured boot, Azure Boost, confidential computing with AMD SEV-SNP/Intel TDX), secure by default (isolated VNets, NSGs, DDoS protection, at-rest encryption, Trusted Launch enabled for Gen2 VMs), and secure in operation (Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Azure Monitor, JIT VM access via Entra ID). The post explains how these layers work together so no single control failure leads to platform-wide compromise.

recent_posts.title: Enforcing trust and transparency: Open-sourcing the Azure Integrated HSM
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft is open-sourcing the Azure Integrated HSM, a tamper-resistant hardware security module built into every new Azure server. Engineered to meet FIPS 140-3 Level 3 standards, it brings hardware-enforced cryptographic key protection directly to the compute layer rather than relying solely on centralized services. The firmware, driver, and software stack are now available on GitHub, with an OCP workgroup planned to guide ongoing development. Keys are designed to never leave the hardware boundary, eliminating entire classes of memory-based key exfiltration attacks. The HSM supports TDISP for integration with confidential computing environments and will be available in Azure V7 VMs globally in the coming weeks.

recent_posts.title: Microsoft named a Leader in the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide API Management 2026 Vendor Assessment
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft has been named a Leader in the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide API Management 2026 Vendor Assessment. Azure API Management supports over 38,000 customers, nearly 3 million APIs, and more than 3 trillion API requests monthly. The platform is expanding beyond traditional API governance to cover AI workloads, offering a unified control plane for managing models, tools, and agents in production. Customer examples include Heineken (50M API calls/month, 100% uptime, 75% cost reduction), Banco Bradesco (centralized AI and API governance for digital banking), Access Group (50+ AI products launched, 2.2M users), and Air India (40,000 daily AI-handled queries). Microsoft positions Azure API Management as a single platform for governing both APIs and AI systems at enterprise scale.

recent_posts.title: OpenAI’s GPT-5.5 in Microsoft Foundry: Frontier intelligence on an enterprise ready platform
recent_posts.summary: OpenAI's GPT-5.5 is becoming generally available in Microsoft Foundry on Azure. The model advances the GPT-5 series with deeper long-context reasoning, more reliable agentic execution, improved computer-use accuracy, and greater token efficiency. A premium GPT-5.5 Pro variant is also available for more demanding workloads. Microsoft Foundry provides the enterprise platform layer for deploying these agents at scale, with support for LangGraph, Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, and GitHub Copilot SDK. Pricing starts at $5/M input tokens and $30/M output tokens for GPT-5.5, with GPT-5.5 Pro at $30/M input and $180/M output tokens.

recent_posts.title: Microsoft Discovery: Advancing agentic R&D at scale
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft is expanding preview access to Microsoft Discovery, its agentic AI platform purpose-built for R&D organizations. The platform combines agentic orchestration, advanced reasoning, a graph-based knowledge foundation, and high-performance computing on Azure to automate scientific discovery loops. Real-world use cases include identifying a novel datacenter coolant in ~200 hours, oncology tumor microenvironment analysis with GigaTIME, accelerated chip design with EDA leader synopsys, and compressed engineering simulation cycles for Microsoft Surface cooling fans via PhysicsX. The platform integrates with Microsoft 365, Azure AI foundry, and Microsoft fabric, and includes governance controls, audit trails, and compliance frameworks for enterprise R&D environments.

recent_posts.title: Introducing Azure Accelerate for Databases: Modernize your data for AI with experts and investments
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft has launched Azure accelerate for databases, a program combining expert guidance, financial incentives, and skilling resources to help organizations modernize their database infrastructure for AI readiness. Key benefits include up to 35% savings via a flexible spend-based savings plan, zero-cost delivery support through Microsoft's Cloud accelerate Factory, Azure credits and delivery funding, and 50% discounts on certification exams. The offering targets organizations moving from legacy database environments to fully managed, AI-optimized Azure databases. Thomson Reuters is cited as a case study, having migrated over 18,000 databases totaling 500TB to Azure SQL managed instance.

recent_posts.title: Optimize object storage costs automatically with smart tier—now generally available
recent_posts.summary: Azure has announced the general availability of smart tier for Azure Blob Storage and Data Lake Storage. Smart tier is a fully managed, automated tiering feature that continuously evaluates object access patterns and moves data across hot, cool, and cold tiers without manual lifecycle rule management. Data inactive for 30 days moves to cool, and after another 60 days to cold; re-access immediately promotes it back to hot. Over 50% of smart-tier-managed capacity has already shifted to cooler tiers during preview. Setup requires only selecting smart tier as the default access tier on zonal-redundancy storage accounts. There are no tier transition, early deletion, or retrieval charges — only a monthly monitoring fee per managed object. Objects under 128 KiB are excluded from tiering. The feature is now available in nearly all zonal public cloud regions.

recent_posts.title: How Drasi used GitHub Copilot to find documentation bugs
recent_posts.summary: The Drasi team (a CNCF sandbox project at Microsoft Azure) built an AI-powered documentation testing system using GitHub Copilot CLI, Dev Containers, GitHub Actions, and Playwright. The system deploys a 'synthetic user' agent that reads tutorials literally, executes every command, and verifies expected outputs — mimicking a new developer with no prior context. Running weekly across isolated containers, the agent found 18 distinct issues including implicit dependencies, missing verification steps, and format drift. The security model isolates the agent inside ephemeral Dev Containers with minimal PAT permissions. The approach converts documentation maintenance from a manual chore into an automated monitoring problem, effectively giving a four-person team a tireless QA engineer.

recent_posts.title: Azure IaaS: Keep critical applications running with built-in resiliency at scale
recent_posts.summary: Azure IaaS provides built-in resiliency capabilities across compute, storage, and networking to help organizations keep critical applications running during disruptions. Key features include Virtual Machine Scale Sets with availability zones for compute isolation, multiple storage redundancy models (LRS, ZRS, GRS, RA-GRS), and networking services like Azure Load Balancer, Application Gateway, Traffic Manager, and Azure Front Door for traffic continuity. The post emphasizes that resiliency is a shared responsibility: Azure provides the platform foundation while customers design workloads to meet their specific needs. It also covers migration as an opportunity to build resiliency from the start using Azure Site Recovery, Azure Migrate, and infrastructure-as-code practices, and stresses ongoing validation through testing and observability.

top_posts.title: What’s new with Microsoft in open-source and Kubernetes at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon Europe 2026
top_posts.summary: Microsoft's KubeCon + CloudNativeCon Europe 2026 announcements cover advances across open-source AI infrastructure and Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS). Key highlights include Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) graduating to GA, the new AI Runway open-source project providing a common Kubernetes API for inference workloads, HolmesGPT joining CNCF as a Sandbox project, and Dalec for declarative container image builds. On the AKS side, updates span identity-aware networking (Azure Kubernetes Application Network, Cilium mTLS, WireGuard encryption), GPU telemetry integrated into managed Prometheus/Grafana, cross-cluster networking via Fleet Manager with Cilium cluster mesh, shared Elastic SAN storage pools, AKS desktop GA, and safer upgrade mechanisms including blue-green agent pool upgrades and rollback support.
